scientific_conclusion: The checksum-verified Stage-84 pair-face maps show an abrupt suppression at the wall-adjacent interior x faces. Across both retained opposite-sector pairs and both sidewalls, the wall-adjacent L2 amplitude is at most 1.5900% of the first-interior face amplitude, while at least 88.4561% of the first two wall-normal face transitions is concentrated in the wall-to-first jump. The best scaled first-interior shape reproduces each tiny wall vector with at most 1.3087% residual relative to the first-interior amplitude. Raw Pearson correlations range from negative to positive because some wall vectors are nearly extinguished and are therefore diagnostic only. This establishes a frozen near-wall suppression pattern, not a wall-model/reconstruction error, not an adjoint sensitivity, and not evidence that changing transport will improve q_av. The failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint remains unrecovered.
positive_findings: Wall-adjacent, first-interior, and second-interior x-face vectors are compared directly on both sidewalls for both retained opposite-sector pairs.

Amplitude ratios, a scaled-shape residual, raw y correlation, and the fraction of the first two x-face transitions carried by the wall-to-first jump are reported without generating a new solver state.
negative_findings: Raw Pearson correlation is diagnostic only when the wall-adjacent vector is nearly extinguished; the preregistered decision uses amplitude ratios, scaled-shape residual, and jump concentration instead.
A frozen near-wall suppression pattern does not establish a wall-model or reconstruction error and is not an adjoint sensitivity or evidence that changing transport would improve q_av.
The failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint remains unrecovered and is not extended across Knudsen number.
No physical, collision, correction-floor, source-relaxation, transport, wall, normalization, or velocity-quadrature parameter is retuned, and no cavity solver is rerun.
